title: Gold as a reserve asset and Singapore's pitch to become a gold trading hub
what_it_is: An adjournment motion debate in which Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat set out a five-part proposal for Singapore to build a gold custody, refining and trading hub, followed by a response from Minister Chee Hong Tat on MAS's financial sector development work.
why_it_matters: The transcript states that Singapore's financial sector contributes around 14% of gross domestic product in 2025 and employs almost 200,000 people, more than 80% of whom are locals, with about 90% of net jobs created over the past decade going to locals. Mr Tiong's proposals on gold custody law, refining capacity and market standards were put forward as suggestions, and Mr Chee said he would take them on board. The record does not set out any decision taken on those proposals.

key_points.point: The Leader of the House moved that Parliament adjourn.
key_points.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
key_points.quote: That Parliament do now adjourn.

key_points.point: Mr Tiong argued that gold, not the US dollar, is the reserve asset now seeking an offshore home.
key_points.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
key_points.quote: the emerging reserve asset seeking an offshore home is not dollars. It is gold.

key_points.point: Central bank gold buying has run above 1,000 tonnes a year for three years.
key_points.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
key_points.quote: Gold purchases have exceeded 1,000 tonnes annually for three consecutive years, more than double the 2010 to 2021 average.

key_points.point: He cited a World Gold Council survey of central bank expectations on dollar and gold holdings.
key_points.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
key_points.quote: 73% of central banks expect fewer US dollar holdings over five years; 95% expect to increase gold over 2025 to 2026.

key_points.point: He said the gold price passed $5,000 an ounce in January.
key_points.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
key_points.quote: And gold crossed $5,000 in January.

key_points.point: He described a trend of central banks moving gold out of the Bank of England.
key_points.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
key_points.quote: In 2024, India repatriated 100 tonnes of gold from the Bank of England to domestic vaults – its largest movement since 1991.

key_points.point: He said World Gold Council statistics show Singapore was a large net seller of gold in 2025.
key_points.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
key_points.quote: Singapore was the second-largest net seller at 10 tonnes, behind Uzbekistan

key_points.point: He said MAS disclosures show a fall in gold holdings over a year.
key_points.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
key_points.quote: gold holdings fell by 849,000 troy ounces from January 2025 to January 2026

key_points.point: He asked the Government to confirm the reported gold sales.
key_points.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
key_points.quote: could the Government confirm whether this is true?

key_points.point: First proposal: a law giving custody arrangements legal certainty.
key_points.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
key_points.quote: Singapore should consider a Reserves Custody Protection Act, or an amendment to the MAS Act, establishing that custody arrangements are governed by Singapore law and due process, immunising it from executive discretion.

key_points.point: Second proposal: Singapore should hold more gold rather than sell.
key_points.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
key_points.quote: If 73% of central banks expect to increase gold holdings, Singapore should be among them, not amongst the sellers.

key_points.point: Third proposal: expand refining capacity and build direct relationships with miners.
key_points.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
key_points.quote: We should expand refining capacity and establish direct relationships with miners in Africa, Australia, Indonesia, and strengthen existing ones with the bullion banks.

key_points.point: Fourth proposal: create a Singapore standard-setting body for bullion.
key_points.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
key_points.quote: Create a Singapore Bullion Standards Authority.

key_points.point: Fifth proposal: revive a gold lending benchmark and the derivatives it supports.
key_points.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
key_points.quote: we should revive the GOFO, the Gold Forward Offered Rate, and the derivatives architecture it enables.

key_points.point: He said gold investment demand in Singapore is already rising.
key_points.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
key_points.quote: In the second quarter of 2025, gold investment in Singapore surged 37% year-on-year.

key_points.point: He cited inflows into a Singapore-listed gold ETF.
key_points.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
key_points.quote: SPDR Gold Shares recorded S$309 million in net inflows in the first half of 2025 – the highest of any Singapore-listed Exchange Traded Fund (ETF).

key_points.point: He said CPF members' gold investments through that ETF are held in London and New York vaults.
key_points.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
key_points.quote: Central Provident Fund members investing in gold through SPDR Gold Shares will see that gold held in London and New York vaults.

key_points.point: He described Singapore's existing gold infrastructure as limited.
key_points.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
key_points.quote: Singapore's gold infrastructure, with respect, is minimal.

key_points.point: Mr Chee said he shares the ambition set out in the speech.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
key_points.quote: There is no disagreement with what he has laid out in terms of our ambition.

key_points.point: Mr Chee gave the financial sector's contribution to GDP.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
key_points.quote: our financial sector contributes around 14% of gross domestic product in 2025

key_points.point: Mr Chee gave the sector's average annual growth from 2021 to 2025.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
key_points.quote: Between 2021 and 2025, it grew at an average of 4.6% annually

key_points.point: Mr Chee gave the sector's employment numbers and local share.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
key_points.quote: Today, the financial sector employs almost 200,000 people, more than 80% are locals.

key_points.point: Mr Chee said most net jobs created in the sector over the past decade went to locals.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
key_points.quote: Over the past decade, the Singapore financial sector workforce grew by more than 40,000 – and about 90% of the net jobs created went to locals.

key_points.point: Mr Chee said Singapore and Dubai can both operate as financial centres.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
key_points.quote: It is not a zero sum.

key_points.point: Mr Chee cited digital bank licences as an example of adapting policy.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
key_points.quote: we granted banking licences to four digital banks

key_points.point: Mr Chee described the FinTech Regulatory Sandbox.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
key_points.quote: our FinTech Regulatory Sandbox, which enables firms to experiment with innovative products and business models in a controlled regulatory environment

key_points.point: Mr Chee gave figures for Singapore's fund management sector.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
key_points.quote: more than 1,200 licensed fund management companies managing over $6 trillion in assets

key_points.point: Mr Chee gave Singapore's ranking and daily volume in foreign exchange.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
key_points.quote: Singapore is also the third largest foreign exchange centre in the world, with over US$1.4 trillion traded here every day.

key_points.point: Mr Chee said MAS has supported the setting up of innovation labs.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
key_points.quote: MAS has supported the establishment of over 15 innovation labs

key_points.point: Mr Chee gave the number of finance professionals trained in sustainable finance.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
key_points.quote: we have trained over 8,000 finance professionals in sustainable finance

key_points.point: Mr Chee said he welcomes the gold market suggestions.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
key_points.quote: I do welcome the suggestions that Mr Tiong mentioned earlier about the gold market.

key_points.point: Mr Chee said he will consider whether the ideas can be implemented to strengthen Singapore as a gold trading hub.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
key_points.quote: I will take on board what he has mentioned in his speech to see whether those are ideas that we can also implement to strengthen our position here as a gold trading hub.

key_points.point: Mr Chee described the approach for the gold market and other financial segments.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
key_points.quote: work closely with the industry, listen to feedback, be open to new ideas and then take calculated risks and be willing to move, be willing to make bold decisions.

key_points.point: Mr Chee said some initiatives may not succeed but should still be attempted.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
key_points.quote: Some of the things that we try may not succeed, but we must try.

what_happens_next: Parliament adjourned at 5.29 pm. Mr Chee said he will take on board the gold market suggestions to see whether they can be implemented to strengthen Singapore's position as a gold trading hub.
not_said: Whether MAS sold gold in 2025 and on what basis, which Mr Tiong asked the Government to confirm.
Whether the Government will introduce a Reserves Custody Protection Act or amend the MAS Act.
Whether Singapore will establish a Singapore Bullion Standards Authority or an Asian Good Delivery standard.
Whether a GOFO-equivalent benchmark will be revived.
Whether MAS will increase its own gold holdings.
What specific policies, if any, MAS will adopt for the gold market and on what timeline.
